section.title: Activity
section.para: Some checkers are lined up, with blue on one side, red on the other, and 1 empty space between them. A move in this checker game pushes any checker forward 1 space, or jumps over any 1 checker of the other color. Jumping the same color is not allowed, moving backward is not allowed, and 2 checkers cannot occupy the same space.

image.alt: THREE BLACK CHECKERS, A SPACE, AND THEN THREE RED CHECKERS.

section.para: You complete the puzzle by switching the colors completely: ending up with black on the right, red on the left, and 1 empty space between them.

list.item: Using 1 checker on each side, complete the puzzle. What is the smallest number of moves needed?
Using 3 checkers on each side, complete the puzzle. What is the smallest number of moves needed?
Estimate the number of moves needed if there are 2 or 4 checkers on each side. Then test your guesses.

div.para: The moves that don’t involve the fourth checker on each side are the same as before, so it is possible to decide the number of moves by running the first half of the three-checker game, then moving the fourth checkers, and then running the second half.

list.item: Noah says he used the solution for 3 checkers on each side to help him solve the puzzle for 4 checkers. Describe how this might happen.
How many moves do you think it will take to complete a puzzle with 7 checkers on each side?
